limitations: Repeated trials in one person, not independent people. Randomization and blinded assessor masking were not established.

statement: Fusiform stimulation does not establish a unitary face center: nonspecific nonface changes occurred, naming tests were small and procedurally different, current can affect connected sites, and the two stimulated regions were not separated.
source_locators: Methods: famous face/place naming; Discussion paragraphs 2–4
alternative_explanations: A distributed circuit containing these sites is compatible with the effect.
limitations: Famous-face naming errors: 1/5 real, 2/5 sham; places: 2/5 real, 0/5 sham. Null naming differences are not equivalence. No seizure or after-discharge was reported during stimulation.

statement: Scheinin et al. recruited 40 healthy young men; 39 underwent randomized open propofol (19) or dexmedetomidine (20) anesthesia and 37 returned for sleep after two withdrawals. These are overlapping arms, not 76 participants.
source_locators: Methods: Subjects and Experimental designs; Results: Physiologic sleep
alternative_explanations: Within-person control strengthens comparability without creating independent replications.
limitations: One propofol participant withdrew after randomization. Sleep occurred on average 18 weeks later; eligibility was restricted to healthy right-handed men aged 20–30.

statement: Among interviewable states, Scheinin et al. reported subjective experience in 80% of anesthesia interviews and 71% of sleep interviews, including contentless impressions; these are interview rates, not population prevalence.
source_locators: Results: Realization of experimental designs; Assessment of the state of consciousness
alternative_explanations: Dreaming and memory incorporation, with report and memory selection, can produce these reports.
limitations: Exact interview numerators and denominators for these percentages are not supplied in the inspected main text. Later prose shifts the 80% figure to arousable subjects; this remains a unit inconsistency. No extrapolation to deep unarousable anesthesia.

statement: State-linked relative PET blood-flow changes involved thalamic, cingulate and angular regions; fixed infusion and within-subject awakenings improved the comparisons, but these remain neural associations within manipulated states, not focal necessity or sufficiency tests.
alternative_explanations: Arousal, attention, motor access, reporting and memory can contribute.
limitations: Disconnection contrasts: propofol 19, dexmedetomidine 14, sleep 9; reconnection: propofol 9, dexmedetomidine 16. Propofol loss used moderate sedation versus UR with different doses because only two reached UR2. PET integrates over 90 seconds.

statement: The anesthesia study notes that absent response or recalled content cannot conclusively establish absent experience or environmental awareness; three awareness-report states were excluded from its disconnected contrasts.
source_locators: Assessment of the state of consciousness; Results: realization; Discussion limitations
alternative_explanations: Memory failure, stimulus salience and output impairment can hide experience.
limitations: One propofol and one dexmedetomidine awareness report followed UR2, and one followed N2 sleep; these need not be three disjoint people across overlapping arms. The initial anesthesia dream question preceded PET, while the detailed interview followed PET.

statement: Tasserie et al. studied five male rhesus macaques: two DBS animals and three awake comparators, with previously published awake auditory data reused. The intervention unit is two animals.
source_locators: Methods: Animals and Event-related auditory task
alternative_explanations: Comparisons cannot remove all differences between DBS animals and separate awake animals.
limitations: Do not pool animals, sessions, voxels or reused datasets. Detailed session counts and exclusions in uninspected supplements remain gaps.

statement: Under maintained propofol, high central-thalamic stimulation increased the reported arousal score from 0/11 to 9/11 in both DBS macaques; low CT reached 3/11 and ventrolateral stimulation remained 0/11. This supports causal modulation of behavioral arousal under these conditions.
source_locators: Results: Behavioral effects; Figure 2E; Methods: stimulation protocol
alternative_explanations: Stimulation can recruit widespread axons and arousal pathways rather than only local cell bodies.
limitations: Awake score 11/11; stimulation was 3 V versus 5 V at 130.208 Hz. Behavior was assessed outside the scanner without paralysis. Blinding and randomized condition order were not established in the inspected text.

statement: High CT stimulation also shifted fMRI dynamics and enhanced hierarchical auditory responses, but subjective awareness was inferred from signatures; no auditory VL-control data were acquired and anesthetic fMRI used paralysis.
source_locators: Figure 6; Methods: anesthesia and auditory task; Discussion
alternative_explanations: Arousal, sensory gating or processing may restore markers without proving a specific subjective content.
limitations: Separate awake animals and reused data; passive local-global task, without trialwise experience reports. Medial nuclei and axonal spread, plus physiological changes, limit localization. This is not proof of efficacy in human brain injury.

statement: Cogitate recruited 256 across fMRI (120), MEG (102) and iEEG (34), retaining 108, 97 and 32 respectively. Main noninvasive tests used 73 fMRI and 65 MEG held-out datasets; invasive data were not split.
alternative_explanations: Analysis-specific samples and clinical coverage constrain modality comparisons.
limitations: fMRI exclusions: eight motion, two coverage, two incomplete; MEG: two behavior, two noise, one reconstruction; iEEG: two incomplete. Three iEEG patients below the behavior threshold were retained as a declared deviation. iEEG analyses used 31 for activation, 29 for decoding and 28 for RSA.

statement: Cogitate tested suprathreshold visual category, identity, orientation and duration while varying task relevance; it did not directly contrast conscious with unconscious processing or perturb candidate brain regions.
alternative_explanations: Visible-stimulus responses may include unconscious processing; task irrelevance does not guarantee absence of attention.
limitations: Durations were 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 seconds across four categories. A separate 39-person surprise-memory control supports encoding of irrelevant items but cannot certify continuous awareness of every feature or offset on each main-study trial.

statement: Operational predictions contrasted posterior versus prefrontal decoding, posterior duration tracking versus prefrontal onset/offset ignition, and posterior versus long-range prefrontal synchrony; core mathematical theories were not directly computed or exhaustively tested.
source_locators: Preregistered predictions; Protocol Experiment 1; biological focus
alternative_explanations: Auxiliary biological implementations and measurement assumptions can be revised.
limitations: Prediction centrality differed: IIT decoding was noncritical. The published 2023 protocol is an earlier version, not a complete audit of OSF timestamps.

statement: Results partly supported sustained posterior representations and transient prefrontal category decoding, but the expected prefrontal offset profile and sustained posterior gamma synchrony were not established; no overall theory winner follows.
alternative_explanations: Coverage, macroscopic mixed selectivity, awareness timing and sampling could affect null results.
limitations: PFC orientation decoding appeared only in MEG with leakage uncertainty; identity was absent in PFC and posterior face orientation was not sustained. The outcome is mixed, not total refutation of either theory.

statement: Preregistered pairwise phase consistency supported neither critical connectivity prediction; additional exploratory dynamic functional connectivity partly supported GNWT and still lacked sustained posterior connectivity.
source_locators: Results: Interareal connectivity; Supplement section 14, items 5–8
alternative_explanations: PPC noise and sparse V1/V2 sampling can reduce sensitivity; DFC measures amplitude co-modulation rather than phase.
limitations: Do not relabel DFC as preregistered confirmation. Main fMRI connectivity pooled task conditions. The cited coverage comparison has 12 V1/V2 electrodes versus 472 in PFC, and relevant posterior pair analyses involved only four patients.

statement: The 2023 protocol made offset ignition conditional on conscious detection in its GNW overview and described it as possible in analysis 2; elsewhere it described onset/offset as the tested expectation. This qualifies claims that the later offset objection was entirely post hoc.
source_locators: Protocol GNW overview and Experiment 1 analysis 2; Nature prediction 2
alternative_explanations: Failure of a committed operational test can still challenge the model even when it is not an unconditional whole-theory prediction.
limitations: Original and amended OSF files were not audited; retain the wording tension rather than select a convenient version.

statement: Naccache and colleagues argue that assumptions about offset attention, continuous awareness and macroscopic PFC decoding limit the Nature challenge; they also deny that activity-silent storage is mandatory for GNWT.
source_locators: Critique: offset, decoding and duration sections; Supplement section 13, pp.122–124
alternative_explanations: The consortium argues in the original discussion that strong suprathreshold signals, multimodal controls and prior agreements make failures informative.
limitations: This is a documented argument, not measured inattention. The critique says category and orientation decoding were lacking, although Nature found category decoding; do not adopt that wording as an empirical result. Its name correction does not repair this wording.

statement: IIT proponents accept the failed sustained gamma-synchrony prediction but propose coverage, frequency choice and relaxed ROI criteria as limitations; their posterior-sufficiency interpretation is an argument, not a direct inactivation result.
alternative_explanations: The consortium treats missing connectivity as a substantive challenge; a different frequency cannot count as success of the original gamma prediction.
limitations: No Phi or full cause-effect structure was computed. Posterior localization fits multiple theories; ROI relaxation is acknowledged in supplementary section 14.

statement: The published protocol, final article and supplement disclose analysis changes, including an original half-split versus final one-third optimization split, retained low-performance patients, altered RSA and exploratory DFC; this packet does not claim a verified OSF history.
source_locators: Protocol project status; Nature Participants; Supplement section 14, pp.124–126
alternative_explanations: Transparent deviations can be pragmatically justified while changing confirmatory weight.
limitations: Detailed supplementary analyses were not recomputed, and separate registration files remain uninspected.

statement: Neural perturbations provide causal evidence for contributions to human perceptual reports and macaque arousal/access markers, while PET and theory-test recordings locate associations; they do not establish one universally necessary and sufficient neural mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Models limited to reporting or output remain logically possible but must explain reversible, site-specific reported phenomenological effects.
limitations: Distinct studies, methods and species are not pooled; generalization requires separate validation.

statement: This packet does not establish physicalist identity, fundamentality, universal consciousness, brain-independent survival, timelessness, cosmic purpose, goodness or moral authority; those conclusions need additional discriminating and bridge premises.
alternative_explanations: Identity, psychophysical-law, dualist/interface and idealist accounts can accommodate causal neural dependence when explicitly specified.
limitations: Compatibility is not positive evidence or equal likelihood. No posterior is assigned. H-B does not mean that the brain has no influence.

statement: Lennox argues that explaining a mechanism does not exclude an agent, illustrated by Ford and the engine.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: Lennox advances intelligibility and sophisticated laws as positive reasons for a creator and challenges naturalism’s warrant for reason.

statement: Leibniz states a PSR for true or existent facts and distinguishes necessary truths from contingent truths.

statement: Leibniz argues that even an infinite sequence of contingencies lacks its ultimate reason internally and concludes to a necessary substance.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: Leibniz separately attributes unity, perfection, understanding and will to the foundation, with choice governed by the best.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: In Hume’s Part IX, Cleanthes objects to Demea through conceivability, a possible necessary material universe, and explanation of parts; Philo adds an analogy with hidden necessity.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Speaker attribution; the conceivability premise and causal-priority conception are themselves contestable.

statement: Philo challenges extrapolation from human artifacts and asks what a mental plan explains; Cleanthes replies that explaining a cause does not require explaining its cause.

source_locators.locator: Parts II,IV,V; especially Part IV pp21–23

statement: Collins presents fine-tuning as comparative support over an atheistic single-universe hypothesis, explicitly short of proof or an all-things-considered verdict.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: Collins motivates life under theism through divine goodness and the value of intelligent conscious beings.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: Collins distinguishes epistemic probability from metaphysical necessity when answering the deeper-law objection.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.

statement: Collins answers anthropic dismissal by treating our existence as evidence and says unexplained designer complexity need not cancel comparative likelihood support.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: These responses do not settle selection, prior probability or the truth of likelihood premises.

statement: Weisberg distinguishes old knowledge of life from newly learned stringency and questions the extra evidential contribution of stringency.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Not a claim that the initial existence of life cannot favor design.

statement: Weisberg derives screening-off from matched divine and blind indifference distributions, with divine intent used in his larger argument.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Conditional model, not a measure-free refutation of all design hypotheses.

statement: Weisberg allows initial life evidence to support design and acknowledges problems involving uniformity, unbounded spaces and parameterization.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Replies by White and Bradley are mediated; later replies not independently inspected.

statement: Agency compatibility does not itself favor agency; intelligibility can favor a rational creator if independently motivated comparative expectations differ.
alternative_explanations: Impersonal necessary structure; selection-and-learning proposal with empirical adequacy untested here.
limitations: Our reconstruction, not a direct quotation. No equation equates nonintentional origins with unreliable reason.

statement: A restricted PSR covering contingent totality, noncircular external explanation and a concrete-ground premise conditionally yield necessary concrete reality; mentality needs further premises.
alternative_explanations: Brute totality; necessary impersonal ground; rejection of concrete-ground premise.
limitations: Our explicit reconstruction; totality contingency not inferred merely from contingent parts. Modal necessity is not temporal or causal priority.

statement: Fine-tuning can supply conditional qualitative comparative support without a numerical posterior; sensitivity alone identifies neither a measure nor designer preferences.
alternative_explanations: Independently motivated deeper constraint or multiverse/selection model; matched conditional distributions.
limitations: Our comparison. Missing numerical inputs do not logically imply no evidential force. Correct Bayes identity is ours; excerpt endnote2 is malformed.

statement: The inspected existence/design routes do not by themselves establish universal subjecthood, human brain independence, survival, timelessness, preservation, goodness or moral authority.
alternative_explanations: Additional independently defended premises may support stronger packages.
limitations: Our entailment assessment under T01 definitions; not a claim that no evidence for these components exists anywhere.

statement: The cumulative use of these arguments must retain shared order, PSR and agent-preference dependencies rather than multiply them as independent observations.
alternative_explanations: A later dependence model could identify genuinely distinct conditional contributions.
limitations: Our method assessment. No independent empirical observations added by author agreement or repeated illustrations.

statement: Einstein’s kinematic argument uses a relativity principle, invariant vacuum light speed and clock synchronization to derive frame-dependent distant simultaneity.
alternative_explanations: A preferred metaphysical frame requires added structure beyond the inspected formulation.
limitations: Reliable theoretical attribution, not a newly reviewed experiment or proof of a unique ontology.
epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

statement: Einstein’s §3 transformation and §4 moving-clock relation retain elapsed clock readings; unequal rates do not eliminate temporal succession.
source_locators: §3 final transformation; §4 moving clock at x=vt
alternative_explanations: Additional ontology may interpret the same measured relations differently.
limitations: Sub-luminal inertial-motion domain; no modern precision test audited.

statement: In the displayed Lorentz relation, positive elapsed time along x=vt remains positive for |v|<c; a complete-history representation therefore need not collapse ordered clock events into one simultaneous event.
alternative_explanations: Whether all represented events equally exist is an additional metaphysical issue.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

statement: Rovelli distinguishes measurable partial observables from predictive complete correlations and treats physical clocks relationally.
limitations: Attribution of this formalism’s interpretation; not a measurement of foundational consciousness.
epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

statement: Rovelli’s constrained formulation does not require privileged external time; §VI explicitly restricts its detailed development to finite degrees of freedom while retaining histories and relational predictions.
limitations: A theoretical framework, not an empirically confirmed complete quantum-gravity cosmology.
epistemic_scope: Attribution of an inspected theoretical construction, not an observed event or empirical confirmation.

statement: Neither coordinate-invariant observables nor omission of privileged external time entails absence of physical change, experience, or all intrinsic succession.
source_locators: §V equation(5) and clock example; §VII; author bridge assessment
alternative_explanations: A further ontology could posit a timeless foundation, but would need independent justification.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

statement: In Boethius V.6, Philosophy contrasts whole possession of life with endless sequential existence and places divine priority in simplicity rather than earlier duration.
limitations: Historical argument attribution; “single moment” in this translation is read with its explicit contrast to temporal succession, not as a coordinate instant.

statement: Boethius IV.6 distinguishes unified providence from its temporal unfolding; V.6 distinguishes conditional from simple necessity in replying to the foreknowledge objection.
source_locators: IV.6 providence/fate distinction; V.3 objection; V.6 knowledge/necessity reply
alternative_explanations: The account still owes an adequate relation between infallible knowledge, grounding and free choices.
limitations: Argument attribution, not an established solution to freedom, evil or providential action.

statement: Craig’s tensed-fact objection is conditional on objective A-theoretic tense and a knower’s need to know what is presently true; he explicitly says a B-theory avoids this argument.
source_locators: Opening numbered argument; paragraph beginning The B-theorist; conclusion
alternative_explanations: Deny irreducible tensed facts or defend atemporal knowledge of them.
limitations: The disputed semantics and knowledge premise are not proven by the existence of a temporal world alone.

statement: Craig argues that replacing propositional beliefs with direct intuition does not by itself remove the objection if irreducibly tensed reality still must be known.
source_locators: Omniscience Despite Ignorance of Tensed Facts; arguments4′ and4*
alternative_explanations: A defender can instead reject absolute presentness or justify a distinct access relation.
limitations: Craig’s objection is directly inspected; his accounts of modern defenders are not substitutes for their originals.

statement: Craig’s personhood defense focuses on a God without temporal creation, distinguishing possible changeless self-awareness from interaction with temporal persons.
source_locators: Opening scope; Criteria Based on States of Consciousness
limitations: Possible personhood without creation is not proof of timeless responsiveness in the actual world.

statement: Craig defends timeless volition by disputing that every intention is future-directed or reached by deliberation; the response invokes a possible unchanging will.
alternative_explanations: A critic may require agency to involve action or reasons responsive capacities whose timeless realization is still unexplained.
limitations: Counterexamples within temporal human life do not by themselves exhibit an actually timeless agent.

statement: Craig also presents a model timeless without creation and temporal with creation; it is a temporal alternative once a world exists, not foundation-level H-T throughout that relation.
source_locators: States of Consciousness, Ockhamist model paragraphs; Inter-personal Relations
alternative_explanations: An atemporal foundation can instead deny the need for intrinsic change upon creating.
limitations: Explaining the relation without a literal temporal “before time” remains necessary; no cosmic clock identification adopted.

statement: A conditional M2 model can posit one non-successive act that knows and grounds a temporally ordered history, provided the grounding relation and individuated subjectivity are independently intelligible.
source_locators: IV.6/V.6; Craig scope; author reconstruction in report
alternative_explanations: An impersonal relational structure or a temporal conscious foundation could realize comparable physical history.
limitations: Project reconstruction, not either source’s verbatim model or proof of full metaphysical coherence.

statement: Knowing a dated event and each person’s indexical belief need not mean being that person or successively acquiring those beliefs; whether this exhausts knowledge of objective presentness is disputed.
source_locators: Craig tensed-fact sections; personhood self-consciousness passage; author reconstruction
alternative_explanations: A-theoretic presentness may demand a genuinely changing cognitive relation.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

statement: A changing time-indexed relation to a fixed foundation is distinct from a new intrinsic state of that foundation; the claim that every genuine response needs such a new state requires argument.
alternative_explanations: Responsiveness understood as new awareness or deliberative revision entails succession.
limitations: Counterfactual dependence across possible histories is not a sequence of changes within one foundation.

statement: M1 temporal continuation, M2 a timeless foundation with temporal persons, and M3 complete-history inclusion are distinct; inclusion of a finite life or its record alone does not meet H-S.

alternative_explanations: A richer M3 must specify same-person subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary.
limitations: Internal conceptual inference under T01; personal identity adjudication deferred to T13.

statement: Relativity, a relational formalism and eternalism do not alone identify an experiential bearer or the grounding relation needed for H-F, H-U, H-T or human survival.
alternative_explanations: Independent philosophical arguments could supply a bridge; these physical formalisms do not supply it by themselves.
limitations: Conditional scope; does not establish actual timeless consciousness.

statement: If rival metaphysical models yield the same physical and report predictions, those observations cannot distinguish them; a discriminating test requires independently specified differing expectations.
source_locators: Author discrimination analysis; reviewed T08/T09 report boundaries
alternative_explanations: A specified interaction model might predict additional measurable differences.
limitations: No assertion that all possible timeless and temporal models are empirically equivalent.

statement: The Boethian and Craig discussions share premises about knowledge and personhood; they are not independent observations, and conditional coherence does not establish actuality or equal support for alternatives.
alternative_explanations: Additional independent evidence may change comparative support.
limitations: No quantitative metaphysical posterior or cumulative nine-component verdict.
